descriptionChirho: A Hebrew masculine noun (מַטְעָם) meaning 'delicacy, dainty food, savory dish', derived from the root טעם 'to taste'. Used primarily in Genesis 27 for the savory food Isaac asked Esau to prepare (Gen 27:4,7,9,14,17,31) and in Proverbs 23:3,6 for deceptive delicacies. Multilingual signatures are uniform: eng 'delicacies/his-delicacies', spa 'manjares/sus-manjares', arb 'أطعمة-شهية/لأطعمته', kor '별미/진수성찬', swa 'chakula-kitamu/vyakula-vyake-vitamu', hin 'स्वादिष्ट-भोजन'. The suffixed form (S111143, 'his delicacies') is a grammatical inflection of the same noun sense as the absolute/construct forms (S111142).
